meta.dataset: Pakistan Public Corruption Atlas — sample seed
meta.disclaimer: This project aggregates publicly available information from reputable and official sources for research, transparency, and educational purposes. Inclusion in the database does not imply guilt. Users should consult the cited primary sources and court records for authoritative information.
meta.note: Sample records summarize publicly reported proceedings. Amounts are as reported by cited sources and may be alleged/estimated. Status fields reflect documented procedural stages, not determinations by this project.

scandals.title: Rental Power Plants (RPP) contracts — alleged irregular procurement
scandals.summary: Public reporting and subsequent accountability proceedings examined alleged irregularities in short-term rental power plant contracts awarded during a period of power shortages. Reporting described questions over pricing, contract awards, and due diligence. Legal and political outcomes evolved over years; this record tracks publicly documented stages and does not assert guilt.

Pakistani politically exposed persons appeared in reporting; subsequent domestic judicial proceedings (including the Panama Case) addressed questions arising from those disclosures. This record classifies the originating material as investigative journalism and separately notes later official proceedings. Offshore ownership disclosures are not themselves proof of corruption.

scandals.title: Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) — governance crisis, alleged mismanagement, and FIFA normalisation
scandals.summary: Since the mid-2010s, Pakistani and international reporting has documented a prolonged governance crisis at the Pakistan Football Federation, including disputed leadership, court involvement characterised by FIFA as third-party interference, headquarters takeovers, and repeated FIFA suspensions. Coverage has also described concerns about administration of federation affairs and accounts during contested periods. This record tracks the publicly reported crisis as it relates to a national sports body receiving public attention and international oversight; it does not assert criminal guilt for any named individual.
scandals.amount_notes: Public reporting focuses on governance interference and control of accounts/premises more than a single adjudicated loss figure.
scandals.court_name: Domestic courts (election/leadership disputes as reported) / FIFA oversight

scandals.title: PFF headquarters takeover (2021) — alleged forced handover of premises and accounts
scandals.summary: In March 2021, Al Jazeera and Pakistani press reported that the FIFA-appointed PFF Normalisation Committee chair said a group linked to contested leadership forced handover of PFF accounts and cheque books after entering federation premises in Lahore. scandals.title: Mehran Bank scandal (Mehrangate) and Asghar Khan case — alleged ISI election financing
scandals.summary: Publicly documented proceedings and press reporting describe the Mehran Bank scandal and the related Supreme Court petition by Air Marshal (Retd.) Asghar Khan. Reporting and court processes examined allegations that intelligence and military officials arranged funds — including via banker Younis Habib / Mehran Bank — to support political actors ahead of the 1990 election. The Supreme Court later issued findings in the Asghar Khan case. This record summarises the publicly reported case stream; consult SC judgments for authoritative outcomes regarding specific respondents.
scandals.institution: Mehran Bank / ISI (as alleged in petition and reporting)
scandals.amount_notes: Figures such as ~Rs 140 million appear in public summaries of alleged disbursements; verify against SC record. Not treated here as an adjudicated loss total for all parties.

scandals.title: 1960s–1970s bureaucratic corruption patterns — academic and historical review
scandals.summary: Peer-reviewed historical research examines growth of corruption among Pakistan's bureaucratic elite in the 1960s and 1970s, linking development spending, local-government manipulation under the Ayub period, and later nationalisation/political control reforms under the 1970s PPP government to changing opportunity structures for corruption. This is an academic synthesis record for OSINT periodisation — not a single criminal case. Use it to contextualise later scandals; do not treat it as proof of guilt for named living persons.
scandals.amount_notes: Historical academic analysis — no single case amount.

Nationalisation and bureaucratic reforms analysed as expanding corruption opportunities
